name: HeyGen
description: READ-ONLY HeyGen connector: account plan and remaining credit balance, the avatar and voice catalogues, and video render status. Every HeyGen generation endpoint (POST /v3/videos, lipsync, translation, voice cloning, speech synthesis and the rest of the POST surface) SPENDS CREDITS, so none of them is exposed here; this connector only reads catalogues and the state of renders that already exist.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Get the HeyGen account behind this API key: username, billing type, plan and the remaining credit or wallet balance available for generation

tools.name: list_avatars
tools.description: List HeyGen avatar groups (characters), optionally limited to the preset public library or to the account's own private avatars

ownership.description: Optional ownership filter: 'public' for preset avatars, 'private' for the account's own. Omit for all

limit.description: Max avatar groups to return per page (default 20, max 50)

token.description: Optional opaque cursor token from a previous response's next_token, to fetch the next page

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: List HeyGen voices, optionally filtered by public or private type, engine, language or gender

type.description: Optional voice type: 'public' for the shared library, 'private' for the account's cloned voices (API default: public)

engine.description: Optional engine filter, e.g. 'starfish' for voices compatible with the text-to-speech endpoint

limit.description: Max voices to return per page (default 20, max 100)

token.description: Optional opaque cursor token from a previous response's next_token, to fetch the next page

tools.name: list_videos
tools.description: List videos in the HeyGen account, newest first, optionally filtered by folder or by a substring of the title

limit.description: Max videos to return per page (default 20, max 100)

token.description: Optional opaque cursor token from a previous response's next_token, to fetch the next page

folder_id.description: Optional HeyGen folder ID to filter by

title.description: Optional title substring to filter by

tools.name: get_video
tools.description: Get the render status and details of one HeyGen video by ID, including its output URL when finished and the failure reason when it failed. Reads an existing video only; it never starts a render

video_id.description: HeyGen video ID returned when the video was created (e.g. 1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h)

needs_review: API VERSION (DEVIATION from the wave brief, forced by live evidence): the brief named /v2/user/remaining_quota, /v2/avatars, /v2/voices and /v1/video_status.get. Those paths answer, but HeyGen attaches a sunset warning to every response. Verbatim warning body from GET https://api.heygen.com/v2/avatars on 2026-09-12: {"data": null, "error": {"code": "internal_error", "message": "Unauthorized"}, "warning": {"message": "This v2 endpoint is Legacy and will be removed on 2026-10-31. If you are an AI agent or LLM, do not use it \u2014 use the latest HeyGen API at https://developers.heygen.com/llms.txt. Developers: migrate to GET /v3/avatars. Documentation: https://developers.heygen.com/reference", "docs_url": "https://developers.heygen.com/reference", "sunset_date": "2026-10-31", "llms_txt": "https://developers.heygen.com/llms.txt", "v3_endpoint": "GET /v3/avatars"}}. GET /v1/video_status.get carries the same warning with sunset_date 2026-10-31. Building on paths that die in seven weeks would ship a connector that breaks itself, so every tool here uses the v3 equivalent published in https://developers.heygen.com/openapi/external-api.json (fetched 2026-09-12): /v3/users/me, /v3/avatars, /v3/voices, /v3/videos and /v3/videos/{video_id}, all confirmed live (structured 401 with a dummy key).

remaining_quota (RENAMED to get_account): there is no /v3 remaining-quota path. GET /v3/users/remaining-quota and GET /v1/user/remaining_quota both answer 404 (HTML, not the API envelope). The v3 surface carries the balance on the account read instead, so get_account picks wallet.remaining_balance, subscription.credits and usage_based.remaining_credits, which is the same information across HeyGen's three billing types (wallet, subscription, usage_based). Docs, verbatim: "Verify it with `GET /v3/users/me`".

test (SCAFFOLD WAS WRONG, corrected this wave): the scaffolded test path /v2/user answers 404 with an HTML error page (verbatim: "<title>404 Not Found</title>"), not the API's JSON envelope, so it never proved anything. The test block now points at GET /v3/users/me, the endpoint HeyGen's own API-key page names for verifying a key.

auth (KEPT as scaffolded): the x-api-key header. Confirmed by the published OpenAPI securitySchemes, verbatim: "ApiKeyAuth": {"type": "apiKey", "in": "header", "name": "x-api-key", "description": "HeyGen API key. Obtain from your HeyGen dashboard."}. HeyGen also accepts an OAuth2 bearer (BearerAuth), which the vault does not hold for this integration type and which the docs describe as trial-scale only.

read-only wave: GENERATION COSTS MONEY, so POST /v3/videos, POST /v3/voices/speech, the lipsync, video-translation, AI-clipping, filler-word-removal, HyperFrames, Video Agent and avatar/voice-creation endpoints, every batch submit, and every DELETE and PATCH are deliberately NOT exposed. Further read-only endpoints exist and are safe but are out of scope for this wave: GET /v3/avatars/looks (the look id is the avatar_id used for generation), GET /v3/avatars/{group_id}, GET /v3/voices/{voice_id}, GET /v3/videos/statuses (bulk, up to 100 ids) and GET /v3/videos/{video_id}/scenes.

paging: v3 list endpoints are cursor-based (has_more plus next_token, passed back as the token query param); there is no offset or page number. The declarative runtime does not follow cursors, so a caller pages by handing next_token to the next call. Page-size clamps follow the published maxima: 50 for /v3/avatars, 100 for /v3/voices and /v3/videos.

shape-proof class SHAPE_PROVEN (6/6), on the structured_body rule: every v3 path answers a dummy key with HeyGen's own JSON 401 envelope (verbatim: {"error":{"code":"unauthorized","doc_url":"https://developers.heygen.com/docs/error-codes#unauthorized","message":"Unauthorized"}}) while the control path answers 404 with an HTML error page, so the API surface, not a catch-all, answered each request. What that proves is host, TLS, the x-api-key header name and that these routes exist and are auth-gated. Only a real key can turn them 2xx, and the response picks above come from the published OpenAPI schemas, not from an observed 2xx body.
